title: Actions and Activities Analysis
opening: You say creativity matters. Look at the activities you repeatedly choose, enjoy or avoid, and the situations around them. Compare a possible preference with behavior from other parts of life.

labels.activitiesPrompt: Add an activity when it helps. There is no required number. Include what you enjoy, what you avoid and what else shapes the choice.
labels.furtherPrompt: Try a new example here, or move a known example when it becomes useful for comparison. Keep each example beside the candidate preference.
labels.pattern: What do you repeat, enjoy or avoid?
labels.absorption: When absorbed, what conditions were present?
labels.candidatePrompt: Write a candidate in your own words. Leave it open to change.
labels.sourceExampleText: Coaching, explaining software and clarifying a family decision can point to a preference for helping people understand. Work done to pay necessary bills can reflect a constraint instead of a preference for long work hours.

labels.method: A value is a sustained preference, not a diagnosis. Repeated behavior can reflect enjoyment, necessity, access, roles or other conditions. Compare examples and keep conflicting behavior visible.

source.status: The activities, candidate preference and examples are entered by the learner. They are not a value diagnosis or proof of a stable trait.
